(1) policy gradient methods can be used to learn complex controllers for simulated robots with high-dimensional state spaces; (2) the variance of policy gradients can be reduced by using value functions to estimate the advantage function; and (3) the combination of policy gradient methods with neural network function approximators and trust region optimization can learn complex controllers for high-dimensional systems.

we develop a scheme to reduce variance in policy gradients by using value functions; we use trust region optimization to optimize the policy; we learn policies for a biped getting up from the ground; and we show that our method can scale up to complex 3D locomotor control tasks.

policy gradient methods can be used to solve challenging problems in continuous control, provided that they have a principled scheme for reducing the variance of the policy gradient estimates, and provided that the policy is optimized in a way that is robust to high variance.
